skill.name: humanode-agentlink
skill.description: Link an AI agent wallet to a biomapped human owner, verify active status on Base, and sign approved HTTP requests with AgentLink.

security_audit.summary: Static command-execution and environment-file detections are false positives caused by Markdown and TypeScript examples. Confirmed findings cover external requests and raw private-key access; semantic review also found unpinned package execution, unrestricted signing guidance, and externally consequential partner actions. No prompt-injection text or secret-exfiltration behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions and document provenance or integrity verification before running npx or npm install.
Make KMS, HSM, or external signer use the recommended default. Never log, prompt for, or commit AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY.
Require destination allowlists and explicit approval before signing a new endpoint or sending a state-changing request.
Require explicit user confirmation before content generation, job commissioning, allowance consumption, or social-media engagement.
Require the owner to review and approve linking details, network, and fees before submitting an on-chain transaction.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The setup guidance runs packages through npx and npm without an exact version or integrity check. A changed published package could alter local execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited setup instructions name npx and npm install commands without a version pin. Package resolution is external and mutable.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Destination Request Signing
semantic_findings.description: The documented fetch wrapper attaches an AgentLink header to every request. Without a destination allowlist and approval gate, an agent can authenticate unintended external requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly says the wrapper attaches the header to every request and separately supports header construction for HTTP clients. No destination restriction is documented.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Social Engagement Commissioning
semantic_findings.description: A partner endpoint is described as commissioning an X raid. Triggering coordinated social engagement can create reputational and platform-policy harm.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited endpoint is explicitly labeled as commissioning an X raid. This is an externally consequential social-media action.

semantic_findings.title: Stateful Partner Requests Need Consent
semantic_findings.description: Partner endpoints generate content or commission jobs, including endpoints labeled GET. They need explicit user approval before invocation because requests can consume allowances or create external work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint table describes content generation and job commissioning, while the WURK section documents a challenge flow. These operations have external effects despite their HTTP method.

content.user_title: Link agents to verified human owners
content.value_statement: AI agents need a way to prove accountable ownership during approved external actions. AgentLink connects an agent wallet to a biomapped owner and signs requests with that identity.
actual_capabilities: Creates and uses an encrypted local keystore through the documented CLI.
Links an agent wallet to a biomapped human owner through the registry flow.
Checks whether a linked AgentLink identity is active on Base.
Builds AgentLink authentication headers for approved HTTP requests.
Supports raw-key and external signer integrations in the documented SDK.
Documents supported XONA and WURK partner endpoints.
limitations: Requires a biomapped human owner and an approved Base network transaction.
Active status depends on the owner remaining biomapped.
Partner endpoints, pricing, availability, and terms can change.
Does not replace secret management, destination allowlists, or user approval controls.

use_cases.title: Verify accountable agent identity
use_cases.description: Link an operations agent to its human owner before it performs approved partner actions.

use_cases.title: Authenticate approved partner calls
use_cases.description: Attach AgentLink headers to allowlisted service requests that require a human-backed agent identity.

use_cases.title: Use external signing infrastructure
use_cases.description: Integrate an external signer when enterprise policy keeps wallet keys in managed hardware or key services.

prompt_templates.title: Check requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what I need before linking an agent wallet to a Humanode owner. Include approval and network requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan secure setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a secure AgentLink setup plan using an external signer. Do not request or display private keys.

prompt_templates.title: Review request destination
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed AgentLink request destination and method. Identify side effects and ask for confirmation before signing.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy controlled integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an AgentLink integration with version-pinned dependencies, endpoint allowlists, audit logs, and approval gates for state-changing requests.

output_examples.input: What happens after I link an agent wallet?
output: The owner reviews and approves an on-chain linking transaction.
The agent can then verify active status and sign approved requests.
The owner must remain biomapped for active status.

output_examples.input: Can I use a managed key service?
output: Yes. Use documented external signer support when keys must remain in a KMS, HSM, or secret manager.
Keep signing destinations allowlisted and require approval for consequential requests.

output_examples.input: Can this call partner services automatically?
output: Only after explicit user approval. Content generation, job commissioning, and social engagement can have external effects or consume allowances.

best_practices: Pin package versions and verify provenance before installing CLI or SDK dependencies.
Prefer an external signer and keep private keys out of prompts, logs, and source control.
Allowlist destinations and require explicit approval before linking, signing new endpoints, or creating external work.
anti_patterns: Do not install unpinned packages in production environments.
Do not treat signed GET requests as harmless or idempotent.
Do not sign arbitrary URLs or initiate owner-link transactions without approval.

faq.question: What does AgentLink verify?
faq.answer: It links an agent wallet to a biomapped human owner and can report whether that link is active on Base.

faq.question: Does linking require a transaction?
faq.answer: Yes. The human owner reviews and approves the linking transaction on the supported Base network.

faq.question: Can I use Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. This skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should I store the agent key?
faq.answer: Prefer an external signer, KMS, HSM, or secret manager. Never place raw keys in prompts, logs, or source control.

faq.question: Are partner endpoints safe to call automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review destination and side effects, then obtain explicit approval before requests that create work or consume allowances.

faq.question: What happens if biomapping becomes inactive?
faq.answer: The AgentLink status becomes inactive until the linked owner is biomapped again.
